title: Demodectic Mange in Dogs: Symptoms, Treatment and Is It Contagious?
description: Demodectic mange in dogs: what it looks like, whether it's contagious to humans, why French Bulldog puppies get it and how vets treat it today.

faq.q: Is demodectic mange contagious to humans or other dogs?
faq.a: No. The Demodex mite lives on almost all dogs, and the disease appears when a dog's immune system can't keep it in check. VCA and the Merck Veterinary Manual say it does not spread to people or to other healthy dogs.

faq.q: What does demodectic mange look like?
faq.a: It usually starts as small, round patches of hair loss with red, scaly skin around the eyes, the lips or on the front legs. It typically doesn't itch unless a secondary skin infection develops.

Many localized cases resolve without treatment; generalized cases often respond to veterinary-prescribed antiparasitic therapy. Follow-up is needed to ensure mites and secondary infections are controlled, and relapse remains possible.

faq.q: How do you treat demodectic mange at home?
faq.a: There is no reliable home cure. Oils, vinegar and sulfur products don't reach mites deep in the hair follicles. The effective approach is a vet-prescribed medicine given on schedule, with follow-up skin scrapings.

faq.q: Why does an adult dog suddenly get demodectic mange?
faq.a: Adult-onset demodicosis can be associated with illness or immunosuppressive medications, but it can start before age four and a cause is not always found. A veterinarian should assess the individual dog.
